name: Bryce Canyon National Park
blurb: Pine forest, prairie dogs and mountain lions above the hoodoos.

tip.title: Remove the prairie dogs
tip.text: Prairie dogs mix the soil and feed hawks and snakes. Set Utah prairie dog to -100% and watch the meadow grass, then the hawk and rattlesnake.

sources.title: National Park Service: Bryce Canyon animals

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah prairie dog, Clark's nutcracker). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Strong high-elevation sunlight powers the short growing season of the plateau forests and meadows.
Break down dead wood, leaves, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Quaking aspen
nodes.desc: A leafy tree of the park's highest, coolest areas, listed on Wikipedia with Douglas fir and blue spruce there.

nodes.name: Showy green gentian
nodes.desc: A tall flowering plant of mountain meadows. GloBI records Hunt's bumble bee feeding on it.
A common large grazer and browser of the park, recorded in numbers by GBIF and eaten by mountain lions.
Crosses the forested plateau and open ground in search of food and water, according to the park service.
A small seed- and insect-eating rodent and a frequent prey of hawks and snakes in GloBI records.
Feeds mainly on pine seeds, caches more than it needs, and also eats insects and carrion. It helps spread limber and whitebark pines.
A bumble bee that gathers nectar and pollen from mountain wildflowers, and is a pollinator.
The most recorded bird near the park. An opportunist that scavenges carrion and takes small animals.
A scavenging bird; GloBI records it feeding on dead mule deer and rodents.
A widespread raptor that hunts rodents, birds and snakes; the GloBI records show many prey species from this area.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The main large predator the park lists. Deer are its chief prey in western mountain country.

story: Bryce Canyon in southwestern Utah is not a canyon but a collection of giant natural amphitheaters along the Paunsaugunt Plateau. Frost weathering and stream erosion carved its hoodoos from red, orange and white rock. The rim sits at 8,000 to 9,000 feet, and the park spans three life zones.
matters: Its forests and meadows hold about 1,000 plant species, 59 mammal species and at least 100 bird species. It is much smaller and higher than nearby Zion National Park.
